7 انفتق quasi-pass. of فَتَقَهُ [i. e. it signifies It became slit, rent, rent asunder or open, or divided lengthwise: became disjoined, or disunited: or became unsewed, or unstitched]: (S, * O, Msb, K: *) and ↓ تفتّق is quasi-pass. of فتّقهُ [i. e. it signifies it became slit, &c., much, or in many places, or it is said of a number of things]. (S, * O, K. *) ―
-b2- انفتقت آبَاطُهُ is said of a fat child [meaning His armpits became chapped, or cracked]. (S in art. ضب.) ―
-b3- انفتق الغَيْمُ عَنِ الشَّمْسِ (O, K, TA) i. e. [The clouds became parted asunder, or] became removed, or cleared away, from [before] the sun: (TA:) and عَنِ القَوْمِ [from over the party of men]. (S, O, K.) ―
-b4- انفتقت عَلَيْهِ بَائِقَةٌ (assumed tropical:) [A calamity, misfortune, or disaster, burst upon him]. (S and K in art. بوق, &c.) ―
-b5- انفتقت said of a she-camel, She was seized with a disease, (AZ, O, K,) termed ↓ فَتَقٌ , (TA,) between her udder and her navel, (AZ, O, K,) occasioned by fatness: sometimes in this case she recovers, (AZ, O,) and sometimes she dies. (AZ, O, K.) ―
-b6- See also 5, in two places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
